text:
anya: Quick sync: proposing a compact rollout metadata protocol for cohort-based pinning. saw pain yesterday when a tenant flip caused broad cache invalidations.
maria: yep, clients with local pin caches re-requested at scale. we need a way to signal targeted invalidation + an easy compatibility path.
kevin: idea: introduce cohort_id on snapshots and a lightweight 'delta manifest' that lists affected allocations. clients can subscribe to cohort changes instead of global TTL expiry.
harry: cohort sounds good, but how do we keep metadata small? catalogs are copied into many control-plane caches.
dalia: protobuf + zstd on the wire + store compact base64 in the catalog entry. control plane exposes a resolved manifest url rather than embedding full list.
anya: sketch of metadata fields: snapshot_id, cohort_id, origin, started_at, prune_deadline, affected_prefixes, fallback_order, affinity_weights. keep arrays shallow.
kevin: sample config/proto (rough):
```
message RolloutSnapshot {
  string snapshot_id = 1;
  string cohort_id = 2;
  uint64 started_at = 3;
  uint64 prune_deadline = 4;
  repeated string affected_prefixes = 5;
  repeated string fallback_order = 6;
  map<string, float> affinity_weights = 7;
}
```
harry: runtime behavior: when snapshot created, control plane writes manifest to blobstore and updates catalog entry with manifest_url + cohort_id. cache clients fetch manifest lazily and subscribe to cohort SSE/longpoll.
maria: fallback semantics: control plane exposes fallback_order; router tries in-order until success. but need to avoid cascading retries that blow up downstream. add jitter/backoff and per-request max_fallbacks.
kevin: also add a client header: X-Redwood-Pin: strict|prefer_latest|allow_fallback. default prefer_latest. strict returns 409 if pin not yet available.
anya: prune plan: cohort-level prune window + per-prefix drain. when prune_deadline passes, evict allocations only if allocation.metadata.snapshot_id == snapshot_id and allocation.state == DRAINED. else keep.
dalia: operational notes: run prune as per-tenant leader with rate-limit and batch-size. avoid cross-tenant sweep. use lease TTL and renewals.
ops-bot: alert: router detected 90% increase in fallback attempts for tenant=orbit in last 10m. correlate with cohort rollout=cohort-20260301.
maria: good signal. telemetry we want: gauge active_cohorts, counter fallback_attempts, histogram time_to_consistency (first request routed to new version), and counter cohort_prune_failures.
harry: migration/backfill: scan pin-change events for last 7d and generate cohort manifests for ones with >N allocations. mark prune_deadline relative to previous pin-change time. backfill runs at low qps.
kevin: compatibility: older clients ignore cohort_id but still see catalog manifest_url (fallback to global TTL). we'll include a v1/v2 version field.
dalia: security: manifest urls should be signed short-lived urls; blobstore enforces tenant isolation.
anya: open questions: how big should affected_prefixes be? do we allow wildcard prefixes? and what's sensible default prune windows (2h regular, 12h reserved pool)?
maria: answers: allow wildcard but restrict to tenant-owned prefixes; defaults: 2h default, 12h for reserved/dedicated. add per-tenant override in org settings.
harry: next steps: kevin to draft proto + manifest writeflow, dalia to draft blobstore URL signing & ACLs, maria to draft router retry/backoff policy, anya to draft RFC text. schedule 30m follow-up mid-week. :calendar: :thumbsup:
